quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #19
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: You should drive below the speed limit when:

options.text: Road or weather conditions are not perfect.
You see a police car.
You are entering a highway with other cars.
You are on a four-lane road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road or weather conditions are not perfect.
questions.explanation: Drive below the speed limit when roads are wet, slippery, or visibility is poor. Even if you drive at the posted speed limit, you can get a ticket for driving too fast for the conditions.

questions.question: You must show proof of insurance when:

options.text: Only if you are in a collision.
You are in a collision or stopped by police.
Only if police stop you and give you a ticket.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are in a collision or stopped by police.
questions.explanation: You must have proof of insurance with you while driving. You must show your insurance proof and license to an officer after a traffic stop or collision.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Drive with caution and be ready to stop.
You must come to a complete stop.
Stop only if necessary.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A stop sign is the only eight-sided sign on any road. You must come to a complete stop. You can only proceed when the intersection is clear and safe.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is correct?

options.text: Side mirrors eliminate all blind spots.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
You can see blind spots using your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Large trucks have large blind spots that other drivers should avoid.

questions.question: At an intersection with a flashing red light, you should:

options.text: Slow down and let others go first.
Slow down and drive carefully through.
Stop completely, look both ways, and go when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, look both ways, and go when safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop completely, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, and only go when it is safe.

questions.question: When a traffic light turns green, you should:

options.text: Let pedestrians cross first.
Speed up as fast as possible.
Back up slowly.
Wait for another driver to wave you on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians cross first.
questions.explanation: A green light allows you to go. However, you must first let pedestrians and other traffic clear the intersection.

questions.question: Use your horn when:

options.text: Another vehicle is blocking your way.
It may help prevent a crash.
Another driver makes a mistake.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may help prevent a crash.
questions.explanation: Only use your horn to avoid crashes. Do not use it to tell slow drivers to go faster or get out of your way.

questions.question: Which statement about tires is correct?

options.text: Tires must have good tread and no damage.
Low air pressure makes tires ride more smoothly.
Over-filled tires do not skid on wet roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tires must have good tread and no damage.
questions.explanation: Your tires must have good tread and be free of damage. Check your tires regularly.

questions.question: By driving on South Carolina roads, you agree to take a chemical test if a police officer asks.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: South Carolina has an implied consent law. By driving in the state, you agree to a chemical test for intoxication if requested.

questions.question: Guide signs are ____ signs that show directions and distances.

options.text: Yellow
Red
Green
White

questions.correctAnswerText: Green
questions.explanation: Guide signs have a green background and show directions and distances to destinations. They help drivers navigate unfamiliar areas.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
Change lanes suddenly or without planning.
Check for other vehicles in the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes suddenly or without planning.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, make sure no vehicles are in your way. Check your mirrors and blind spots. Always use your turn signal before changing lanes so other drivers know what you are doing.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection:

options.text: You should always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians should yield to you.
You should never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must let oncoming traffic go first. You must always let pedestrians cross safely.

questions.question: If you experience a tire blowout:

options.text: Take your foot off the gas.
Do not brake suddenly.
Slowly slow down and pull to the side of the road.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If your tire blows out, release the gas pedal and do not brake hard. Gradually slow down, then gently apply the brakes and pull to the side of the road.

questions.question: Emergency vehicles:

options.text: Have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, and flashing lights.
May use a loudspeaker to give you instructions.
May follow each other.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must let emergency vehicles pass. They have the right-of-way when using sirens or flashing lights. Follow any instructions from their loudspeakers. Emergency vehicles often follow each other, so only move forward when the path is clear.

questions.question: A double solid yellow line down the center of a two-lane road means:

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is not allowed.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Solid lines mean you cannot pass other vehicles.

questions.question: When a bicyclist is turning left:

options.text: They may use the left lane.
They may cut through all lanes.
They may wait on the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may use the left lane.
questions.explanation: Bicycles ride on the road with traffic. It is normal to see a bicyclist in the left lane when making a left turn.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Merge right.
Divided highway begins.
Lane ends.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lane ends.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the right lane is ending ahead. Drivers in that lane must merge into another lane.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, you should:

options.text: Stay near the accident scene and move your vehicle to the shoulder if you can.
Report the accident to police within one week.
Go to the nearest phone and call for help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay near the accident scene and move your vehicle to the shoulder if you can.
questions.explanation: After an accident, stop your vehicle and move it off the road if possible. Help anyone who is hurt. Call police right away. Exchange information with other drivers and report the accident to your insurance company.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing with a crossbuck sign but no gates or flashing lights, you should:

options.text: Approach with care and cross only when you are sure no train is coming.
Turn down your radio so you can hear an approaching train.
Wait for a flagger to clear you to cross, if one is present.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Approach all railroad crossings carefully. Cross only when you know no train is coming from either direction. Lower your radio to listen for trains. If a flagger is present, follow their instructions.

questions.question: A broken yellow line between two lanes of traffic means:

options.text: Both lanes of traffic are going in the same direction.
Passing is allowed when it is safe.
Passing is not allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Dashed yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. You may pass when there is no oncoming traffic in the lane you want to use.

questions.question: What is the best way to deal with tailgaters?

options.text: Speed up to increase the distance between you and the tailgater.
Slam on your brakes to get the other driver to back off.
Change lanes or slowly down to let them pass.
Ignore them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or slowly down to let them pass.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors several times each minute to watch for tailgaters or fast-approaching vehicles. If a car is too close behind you, slow down and let it pass. Most rear-end crashes happen because one vehicle follows too closely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No left turn can be made here.
A left turn can be made only after stopping.
All traffic must turn right at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: No left turn can be made here.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a line through it means the action is not allowed. This sign means left turns are prohibited.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks under 18,000 lbs. allowed.
Hill ahead.
Truck stop ahead.
No trucks allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hill ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers that a steep hill is coming up ahead.

questions.question: How long will your license be suspended if you refuse a chemical test requested by a police officer?

options.text: One month.
Three months.
Six months.

questions.correctAnswerText: Six months.
questions.explanation: South Carolina has an implied consent law. By driving in the state, you agree to be tested for dangerous drugs. If you refuse the test, your license will be suspended for six months. This suspension happens even if you are not convicted of driving under the influence.

questions.question: Why is it important to look far ahead when driving on the highway?

options.text: Helps you keep up with traffic.
Reduces the need for sudden braking or turning.
Allows you to spot upcoming police officers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduces the need for sudden braking or turning.
questions.explanation: Look far ahead on the road to avoid sudden braking or turning. By watching ahead and being ready to stop or change lanes, you can drive more safely, use less fuel, and keep traffic moving at a steady speed.

questions.question: Which of the following blocks the smooth flow of traffic?

options.text: Slowing down to look at a crash.
Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.
Using public transportation instead of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down to look at a crash.
questions.explanation: Slowing down to look at crashes causes traffic jams and should be avoided.

questions.question: To enter a gap in highway traffic, you should:

options.text: Watch only the vehicles behind the gap.
Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
Speed up and let the other vehicles make way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes or entering traffic, make sure no vehicles are in your way. Always check for traffic beside and behind your vehicle before you change lanes.

questions.question: When you see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Stop until the person is far away from the road.
Honk your horn as you pass them.
Carefully drive around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the person is far away from the road.
questions.explanation: South Carolina law protects blind pedestrians. If someone carrying a white cane or using a guide dog enters the street, all drivers must stop and yield to them.

questions.question: On a freeway, you should look farther ahead than on a city street to:

options.text: See potential hazards early.
Account for the distance needed to stop your vehicle.
Keep up with traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: See potential hazards early.
questions.explanation: On the freeway, be ready for changes in traffic. Watch for signals from other drivers. Watch for vehicles merging at on-ramps and be prepared for sudden changes in road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Hospital.
Upcoming intersection.
Railroad crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Upcoming intersection.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs with black symbols alert drivers to situations ahead. This sign warns drivers of an upcoming intersection so they can prepare for traffic or turns.
